title: Command Availability Preconditions

oracle.positive: Unavailable command disabled when wrong selection/document state
oracle.negative: Hidden implementation missing must not appear clickable or mutate doc

reviewer.role: plan gate: this item requires no manual test
reviewer.statement: The plan records manual_test_gate=AUTO_ONLY for every L3 of OM9-L2-01-02, so acceptance rests on the automated checks below; no human item is requested.
reviewer.scope: no on-screen behaviour of its own: the descriptor and the availability rules are pure data

checks_run: RED (behavioural, captured by temporarily restoring the pre-fix gate so the test still compiled): 2 passed; 2 failed. A7 failed in a session where the preconditions WERE met (has_document, selection 2, active view): admit() ignored the context it was handed and used the empty default, so a command that could run was refused. A8 failed because admit() compared option names case-sensitively while the descriptor declares them without case.
GREEN: cargo test -p om9-core --test command_availability -> 4 passed; 0 failed (8 positive cases, 7 negative cases)

cargo test --workspace -j 2: every group ok; cargo check --workspace --all-targets: exit 0
cargo fmt --check: exit 0; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings: exit 0
real windows: tools/validate_m01_l3_003_panels.py -> 7/7 PASS (the application still starts and dispatches)
code_change: capability.rs: Preconditions { needs_document, needs_selection, needs_active_view } on the descriptor, and ContextState { has_document, selection, has_active_view } as the session facts.
capability.rs: availability_with(id, context) checks the preconditions first, in a fixed order, and returns the reason; availability(id) keeps its meaning by delegating with an empty context.

capability.rs: admit_with(id, kind, options, phase, context) is the gate that takes the real context; admit() delegates with an empty context (no context claimed => a command that needs one is refused rather than run blind).
capability.rs: admit() now reads options through Operation::option, so the gate and the descriptor agree about a name's case.
